definitions.cash: Cash means deposits and money market funds with daily dealing. Government bills under three months count as cash.
definitions.lookThrough: Look-through means a parent and any company it controls count as one issuer, including holdings reached through funds.
definitions.measurement: Everything is measured at market value on the measurement date, after trades settle.
definitions.ratings: Where two agencies disagree, the lower rating applies. Notches are counted from AAA: A- is seven notches.

context.note: Invented portfolios and an invented policy. The rules are written the way policies are written, which is the point of the demo.

items.rule: No single issuer may exceed 8% of the portfolio at any measurement date.
No single issuer may exceed 10% on a look-through basis, treating a parent and its subsidiaries as one issuer.
The five largest holdings together may not exceed 35%.
No sector may exceed 25% of the portfolio.
Financials may not exceed 30%, counting banks, insurers and asset managers together.
Exposure to any one country outside the home market may not exceed 20%.
The average credit rating of the bond sleeve must be A- or better.
No more than 5% may be held in bonds rated below investment grade.
Unrated issues may not exceed 2%.
At least 80% of the portfolio must be sellable within five business days at normal volumes.
Cash and cash equivalents must be at least 2% and no more than 15%.
No holding may represent more than three days of its own average trading volume.
